senses.definition: (linguistics, uncountable) The property of indicating the point in time at which an action or state of being occurs or exists.
examples: Dyirbal verbs are not inflected for tense.

senses.definition: (linguistics, grammar, countable) An inflected form of a verb that indicates tense.
examples: English only has a past tense and a non-past tense; it has no future tense.

senses.definition: (grammar, countable, proscribed) A verb form or construction indicating a combination of tense, aspect, and mood.
examples: The "simple present" tense in English can have several meanings.
The Spanish teacher told the student to use the imperfect tense instead of the preterite tense.

senses.definition: (grammar, transitive) To apply a tense to.
Showing signs of stress or strain; not relaxed.
examples: You need to relax, all this overtime and stress is making you tense.
